name: Costello Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Costello Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of pathogenic HRAS gene mutation
Characteristic facial dysmorphisms including coarse facial features, full lips, and large mouth
Cardiac manifestations such as hypertrophic cardiomyopathy or arrhythmias
Global developmental delay or intellectual disability
Loose, soft skin with deep palmar and plantar creases

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Pathogenic HRAS mutation plus presence of at least two major clinical features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Molecular genetic testing is essential for confirmation; clinical features may vary with age.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Coarse facial dysmorphism with full lips and large mouth
searchTerms: coarse facial features with large lips and mouth
distinctive facial appearance with full lips
wide mouth and thick lips with coarse face
HRAS gene mutation causing developmental issues
genetic mutation affecting growth and function
pathogenic mutation leading to clinical symptoms

common.symptomName: Loose, soft skin with deep palmar and plantar creases
searchTerms: loose soft skin with deep hand and foot lines
soft skin with prominent creases on palms and soles
skin laxity with deep palmar and plantar folds

rare.symptomName: Malignant tumors including rhabdomyosarcoma and neuroblastoma
rare.notes: Increased risk compared to general population
searchTerms: malignant tumors of muscle and nerve origin

laboratory: Elevated serum creatine kinase in some cases
imaging: Brain MRI may show nonspecific findings
genetic: Pathogenic mutations in HRAS gene, typically missense mutations
other: Characteristic facial features and skin findings on clinical examination

distinguishingFeatures: PTPN11 or other RAS pathway mutations
Mutations in BRAF, MEK1, or MEK2 genes

redFlags: Development of malignant tumors in infancy or childhood
Severe feeding difficulties with failure to thrive
